name: That Sign Won't Stop Me Because I Can't Read
aka: DW Sign Won't Stop Me Because I Can't Read
That Sign Can't Stop Me Because I Can't Read
look: Two stacked stills from the cartoon Arthur. Top: D.W., Arthur's little sister, peers at a blank orange sign hanging on a wooden door. Bottom: D.W. in her pink dress stands with hands on hips facing the door and its blank sign, with a subtitle along the bottom.
text: That sign won't stop me, because I can't read!
use: The blank sign holds a warning, rule or instruction, and D.W. stands for someone who ignores it out of sheer cluelessness or stubbornness. Used for people who blow right past obvious warnings.
slots: the warning or rule, written on the blank orange sign
label for D.W.: whoever ignores it (optional)
describe: dw from arthur looking at a blank sign on a door
cartoon girl in a pink dress ignoring a warning sign
arthur's sister says that sign won't stop me because i can't read
little aardvark girl with hands on hips in front of a door sign
kid who can't read walks past the warning
origin: D.W. Read, Arthur's little sister, in stills from the PBS animated series Arthur.
